routes.rule:
Routes should only declare the method, URL, schema, and hooks, and connect the route to a controller.
Routes should contain no business logic.

controllers.rule:
Controllers should read the validated request and call appropriate services.
Controllers should contain no business logic.

validation.rule: Validate request bodies, params, query strings, and headers with route schemas instead of manual checks in controllers.
Define response schemas so responses are serialized and do not leak unlisted fields.

hooks_and_decorators.rule: Hooks and decorators shared by routes, such as authentication or loading the current tenant, should live in their own files.

authorization.rule: For authorization, use Policy classes similar to the policy pattern used by Ruby on Rails.

naming.rule: Use filenames such as .routes.ts and .controller.ts where this convention is adopted by the project.

plugins.rule: Register each module as a plugin with its own routes. Use fastify-plugin only for plugins that must share decorators or hooks with the parent scope, such as database clients and authentication.

error_handling.rule: Use a single setErrorHandler as the global exception handler. Controllers and services should throw errors instead of building error responses.

authentication.rule: When user authentication exists, an onRequest or preHandler hook should set request.user with the authenticated user information.

multi_tenancy.rule: When multi-tenancy exists, an onRequest or preHandler hook should set request.tenant with the current tenant information.

request_state.rule: Declare request.user and request.tenant with decorateRequest and type them through module augmentation.

logging.rule: Use Fastify's built-in logger (request.log inside handlers) as the global logger instance.
